319396.title: The crosspolytopal peg conjecture
319396.literal_statement: Let $d\geq 2$, and let $\gamma:S^{d-1}\to\mathbbm{R}^d$ be a smooth embedding of the $(d-1)$-sphere into $d$-dimensional Euclidean space. A **regular $d$-dimensional cross-polytope** is the convex hull of $d$ mutually orthogonal pairs of opposite vertices at equal distance from the center. **Crosspolytopal peg conjecture.** Every smooth embedding $\gamma:S^{d-1}\to\mathbbm{R}^d$ contains the vertices of a regular $d$-dimensional cross-polytope. Guggenheimer proved this claim, but an error in his main lemma appears to invalidate the proof, leaving the problem open.

319714.title: Enumeration of matchings with no 2-left-nestings
319714.literal_statement: Let a matching on $[2n]$ be a set of $n$ disjoint arcs joining pairs of vertices. Assume that $i<j<k<\ell$, and call the arcs $(i,\ell)$ and $(j,k)$ **$m$-left-nesting** when $j-i\leq m$. A $1$-left-nesting is therefore an ordinary left-nesting. Let $\mathfrak{f}_n$ denote the sequence defined in the source. **The 2-left-nesting conjecture.** Among all matchings on $[2n]$, exactly $\mathfrak{f}_n$ have no $2$-left-nestings. The claim is presented as an additional conjecture in the paper's discussion of matching enumeration.

319734.title: Permutation-character conjecture for equivariant Ehrhart series
319734.literal_statement:
Let $P$ be a $G$-invariant lattice polytope, and let $\varphi[t]=\sum_i\varphi_i t^i$ be its equivariant Ehrhart power series. Suppose that $\varphi[t]$ is **effective**, meaning that every virtual representation $\varphi_i$ is an effective representation. Write $\varphi[1]=\sum_i\varphi_i$ for the resulting ungraded character.

**Permutation-character conjecture.** If $\varphi[t]$ is effective, then $\varphi[1]$ is a permutation representation.

The claim is verified in several examples, including simplices, the cube with the symmetric-group action, and the Weyl-group example discussed in the paper. It is not known in general, and effectiveness of an individual coefficient such as $\varphi_1$ does not force that coefficient to be a permutation representation.

319756.title: Novosibirsk 3-color conjecture for planar graphs
319756.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a planar graph. Two cycles are **adjacent** if they have an edge in common. **Novosibirsk 3-color conjecture.** If $G$ has no pair of adjacent $3$-cycles and no pair consisting of an adjacent $3$-cycle and $5$-cycle, equivalently if no $3$-cycle is adjacent to a $3$-cycle or a $5$-cycle, then $G$ is $3$-colorable. This is a conjectural strengthening of known sufficient conditions for 3-colorability of planar graphs. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved, so its status is left open.

319842.title: Buzzard-Lu conjecture on holomorphic domination of K3 surfaces
319842.literal_statement:
Let $X$ be a complex $K3$ surface. It is **holomorphically dominable by ${\mathbb C}^2$** if there exists a holomorphic map

$$
f:{\mathbb C}^2\to X
$$

whose image is dense, equivalently a holomorphic map dominant onto $X$. Let $||\cdot||_\kappa$ denote the Kobayashi-Royden pseudo-metric on $X$.
**Buzzard-Lu conjecture.** Every complex $K3$ surface is holomorphically dominable by ${\mathbb C}^2$. Consequently, its Kobayashi-Royden pseudo-metric vanishes everywhere.
Buzzard and Lu proved holomorphic domination for elliptic and Kummer $K3$ surfaces, but it is unknown for a general $K3$ surface; the vanishing of the Kobayashi-Royden pseudo-metric is likewise open in that case.

320007.title: Kitaev–Remmel conjecture on the generating function for $(2+2)$-free posets
320007.literal_statement:
Let $p_{n,k}$ be the number of unlabeled $(2+2)$-free posets on $n$ elements with $k$ minimal elements, with $p_{0,0}=1$. Define

$$
P(t,z)=\sum_{n\geq 0, k\geq 0}p_{n,k}z^kt^n.
$$

**Kitaev–Remmel conjecture.** The generating function $P(t,z)$ satisfies

$$
P(t,z)=\sum_{n\geq 0}\prod_{i=1}^{n}(1-(1-t)^{i-1}(1-zt)).
$$

This conjecture proposes a simpler form for the generating function that enumerates unlabeled $(2+2)$-free posets by size and number of minimal elements. The supplied text attributes the conjecture to Kitaev and Remmel but gives no information about whether it has been resolved.

320010.title: The duplicate-leaf parse-word conjecture for binary trees
320010.literal_statement: Let $T_1'$ and $T_2'$ be $(n-1)$-leaf binary trees. Let $1 \leq i \leq n-1$, and let $T_1$ and $T_2$ be the $n$-leaf trees obtained from $T_1'$ and $T_2'$ by duplicating leaf $i$. A **parse word** is a word that parses both trees according to the paper's labeling rule. **Duplicate-leaf parse-word conjecture.** There exists a parse word $w = w_1 \cdots w_n$ of $T_1$ and $T_2$ such that $w_i = w_{i+1}$. This would reduce the search for parse words by showing that duplicated leaves can receive the same letter, but the supplied text gives no resolution.

320024.title: The fundamental gap conjecture for convex Schrödinger operators
320024.literal_statement:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded convex domain of diameter $D$, and let $V$ be a weakly convex potential. The Dirichlet eigenvalues $\lambda_1\leq\lambda_2\leq\cdots$ of the Schrödinger operator $-\Delta+V$ then satisfy

$$
\lambda_2-\lambda_1\geq \frac{3\pi^2}{D^2}.
$$

**Fundamental gap conjecture.** The eigenvalues satisfy the inequality above.

The bound asserts that the spectral gap is at least the gap for an interval of length $D$ with zero potential. The paper proves this conjecture, so it is included as solved.

320153.title: The near-acyclic characterization of chromatic threshold zero
320153.literal_statement: A graph $G$ is **near acyclic** if it has a stable set $S$ such that $G-S$ is a forest and every odd cycle has at least two vertices in $S$. **Near-acyclic chromatic-threshold conjecture.** The class of $H$-sub-free graphs has chromatic threshold $0$ if and only if $H$ is near acyclic. This would characterize the graphs whose subgraph-free classes have chromatic threshold zero and would give a gap between thresholds $0$ and $1/3$.

320280.title: Ayyer–Mallick's maximal-degeneracy conjecture for asymmetric annihilation matrices
320280.literal_statement: Let $M_L$ be the Markov matrix of the asymmetric annihilation process on a system of size $L$. The characteristic polynomial has only $2L$ distinct eigenvalues out of a possible $2^L$. **Ayyer–Mallick's maximal-degeneracy conjecture.** The matrix $M_L$ is maximally degenerate in the sense that it has exactly $2L$ eigenvectors. This conjecture is posed as the question of diagonalizability of the Markov matrix after the characteristic polynomial has been determined; the supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.

320408.title: Dominant-eigenvalue pattern conjecture for generalized Petersen limiting curves
320408.literal_statement: For a family of generalized Petersen graphs $G(nk,k)$, let $Q_c(k)$ be the real crossing value and let $\mu_{k+1,\ell,(\ell),\star}$ denote the indicated dominant eigenvalues. **Dominant-eigenvalue pattern conjecture.** For $k\geq4$, the dominant eigenvalue on regions intersecting the real $Q$-axis is given by the five-case formula in the source, and consequently $Q=1,3$ and, when $Q_c(k)>5$, $Q=5$ are isolated limiting points, while $Q=2,4,Q_c(k)$ are non-isolated limiting points. The source says the conjecture is also valid for $k=3$ after omitting the empty $\mu_{k+1,3,(3),\star}$ region, and reports validation for the studied cases.

320558.title: The monotonicity conjecture for the quantum statistical sum
320558.literal_statement:
Let $Z_q(\beta,h)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}e^{-\beta E_n(h)}$ be the quantum statistical sum for the Schrödinger system, where $h>0$ is Planck's constant, $\beta>0$, and $N$ is the dimension of the coordinate space. **Monotonicity conjecture for the quantum statistical sum.** The function

$$
h^N Z_q(\beta,h)
$$

is monotonically decreasing with respect to $h$. This is presented as an additional conjecture beyond the proposed partition-function inequality; the source supplies no resolution. For the homogeneous potentials discussed immediately beforehand, the paper relates this monotonicity to a strict mean-energy inequality.

320583.title: Borcea's normal-matrix spectral-distance conjecture
320583.literal_statement:
Let $A$ be an $n\times n$ normal matrix. Write $W(A)$ for its numerical range, $\Sigma(A)$ for its spectrum, and let $A_k$ be the $(n-1)\times(n-1)$ matrix obtained by deleting the $k$th row and column of $A$. For compact sets, let $H$ denote the symmetrized Hausdorff distance.

**Borcea's normal-matrix spectral-distance conjecture.**

$$
H\left(W(A),\bigcup_{k=1}^n\Sigma(A_k)\right)\leq\min_{c\in\mathbb C}\|A-cI\|.
$$

This is presented as a matrix-theoretic generalization of Schmeisser's conjecture. The source provides no resolution.

320612.title: Uniqueness conjecture for graphs with cyclic defect or excess
320612.literal_statement: A graph with defect or excess $2$ is said to have **cyclic defect or excess** when its defect or excess matrix is the adjacency matrix of a cycle. The Möbius ladder on $8$ vertices is the exceptional graph identified in the paper. **Cyclic defect or excess uniqueness conjecture.** Apart from the Möbius ladder on $8$ vertices, there is no graph with cyclic defect or excess. The authors note that the structural constraints imposed by cyclic defect or excess lead them to believe that this Möbius ladder is the only example; the paper establishes substantial partial results, including finiteness in odd degree, but not the full conjecture.

320663.title: Prolongation intersection conjecture for claw-tree varieties
320663.literal_statement:
Assume the group-based model is abelian. Let $K_{n,1}$ be a claw tree with $n$ leaves, and let $X(T)$ denote the associated variety. A **prolongation** $T_i$ of $K_{n,1}$ is obtained by subdividing an edge so that it has exactly two inner vertices, each of valency at least three.

**Prolongation intersection conjecture.**

$$
X(K_{n,1})=\bigcap_i X(T_i),
$$

where the intersection is scheme-theoretic and ranges over all such prolongations $T_i$ of $K_{n,1}$.

This conjecture gives a geometric description of the claw-tree variety through varieties of two-inner-vertex trees. It is presented as a natural conjecture motivating the method, and no proof or resolution is supplied in the given text.

324670.title: Beck's Chooser-Picker conjecture
324670.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a hypergraph. Suppose that Breaker wins the Maker-Breaker game on $G$, with Maker moving first. **Beck's Chooser-Picker conjecture.** Picker wins the Chooser-Picker game on $G$. This conjecture compares the relative difficulty of the Maker-Breaker and Chooser-Picker games on the same hypergraph. It is refuted by a construction in this paper: there is a hypergraph on which Breaker wins the Maker-Breaker game while Chooser wins the Chooser-Picker game.

333045.title: Cayley conjecture for lattice polytopes of large dimension
333045.literal_statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a lattice polytope of dimension $d$ and degree $s$. A **Cayley polytope** is a lattice polytope expressible as a Cayley sum of lattice polytopes. **Cayley conjecture.** If $d>2s$, then $P$ is a Cayley polytope of at least $(d+1-2s)$ lattice polytopes.

This conjecture concerns how sufficiently high dimension relative to degree forces a lattice polytope to admit a Cayley decomposition, a structure important in the study of lattice polytopes and their algebro-geometric interpretations. Its status is not resolved by the supplied source context.

333045.review_depth: Higashitani v1 Section 5 and v2 Definition 1.5, Conjecture 1.6, Proposition 5.1, Lemma 5.2 and Proposition 5.3 proof passages.
333045.ordinary_attempt_and_prior_status: Binary simplex-code columns force every Cayley block to have ≥3 vertices. For r=1, d=6,s=2 and 7 vertices, at most floor(7/3)=2 blocks while d+1−2s=3. This is a printed source family; no independent witness is new.
333045.precise_gap_or_novelty_limit: No novelty. Source v1/v2 stronger generalized constructions not needed for exclusion; journal body not independently read.
